6.question: Does the AI need to know any specific business rules or definitions to answer questions about your Sales Pipeline topic correctly? Review the pre-populated suggestions below — each was inferred from your selected concepts, datasets, and metrics — then confirm, deselect, or edit any that apply. Use 'Add custom rule' for anything not covered.

selected.label: Opportunities with EXCLUDE_FROM_SALES_PIPELINE = TRUE must be excluded from all pipeline counts, coverage ratios, and forecast calculations
selected.description: The DWH_GTM_OPS_FORECASTING_MODEL contains an EXCLUDE_FROM_SALES_PIPELINE boolean column. When TRUE, the opportunity must not appear in any pipeline volume, attainment, or forecast query, regardless of its stage or close date.
selected.ai_reasoning: EXCLUDE_FROM_SALES_PIPELINE is an explicit `filtered-by` edge on the Sales Forecasting concept selected in Step 2 — failing to apply this filter is the most common cause of overstated pipeline coverage.

selected.label: SALES_DEFINED_FORECAST categories: Commit = high-confidence close this quarter; Best Case = possible close; Pipeline = active but early-stage; Omit = intentionally excluded from forecast
selected.description: The SALES_DEFINED_FORECAST column in DWH_GTM_OPS_FORECASTING_MODEL drives all forecast roll-ups. The in-quarter forecast = Commit + Best Case. 'Omit' deals remain in pipeline volume but are excluded from the forecast number.
selected.ai_reasoning: SALES_DEFINED_FORECAST is a `derives-from` edge on the Sales Forecasting concept and is the primary classification column powering quarter-end forecasts — without these definitions the AI cannot correctly answer 'what is the forecast?'.

selected.label: Pipe Gen = net-new opportunities created in a period (measured by CREATED_DATE). Reactivated, recycled, or re-opened deals must NOT be counted as new Pipe Gen.
selected.description: Pipeline generation is triggered by a new Salesforce opportunity record creation, not by stage entry or re-qualification of a previously closed/lost deal. Recycled opportunities inflating Pipe Gen is a known data quality issue to guard against.
selected.ai_reasoning: Pipe Gen is the primary metric selected in Step 4 with a `measured-by` edge to the Sales Pipeline concept — a creation-date-based definition prevents the AI from double-counting reactivated deals in pipeline generation queries.

selected.label: Pipeline = open (not yet closed) opportunities only. Closed-won deals = Bookings, which belongs to a separate topic. Never mix pipeline volume and bookings figures in the same calculation.
selected.description: The graph explicitly marks Sales Pipeline and Sales Bookings as `distinct-from` concepts. Pipeline covers active deals progressing through stages; Bookings covers realised new-revenue commitments from closed-won deals. Attainment calculations should always clarify which they reference.
selected.ai_reasoning: Sales Bookings has an explicit `distinct-from` edge to Sales Pipeline in the knowledge graph — this rule prevents the AI from blending open pipeline with closed-won bookings in coverage or quota-attainment queries.

selected.label: Pipeline ≠ Forecast. The pipeline is ALL open opportunities; the forecast is the SUBSET classified as Commit or Best Case in SALES_DEFINED_FORECAST that the team expects to close this quarter.
selected.description: When a user asks 'what is the forecast?', route to DWH_GTM_OPS_FORECASTING_MODEL filtered to Commit + Best Case for the current EVALUATION_QUARTER. When asked 'what is in the pipeline?', use the full opportunity-level datasets without forecast-category filtering.
selected.ai_reasoning: Sales Forecasting has a `distinct-from` edge to Sales Pipeline and shares the Pipeline Movement Dashboard dataset with it — this rule prevents the AI from conflating total pipeline volume with the committed forecast number.

selected.label: Use EVALUATION_QUARTER (not CLOSE_DATE) to assign a deal to an in-quarter forecast. If a deal slips, EVALUATION_QUARTER is updated; CLOSE_DATE may lag behind.
selected.description: When deals miss their original close date, the EVALUATION_QUARTER in the forecasting model is revised to the new target quarter while the Salesforce CLOSE_DATE is often only updated after the sales rep acts. For in-quarter pipeline and forecast questions always filter on EVALUATION_QUARTER.
selected.ai_reasoning: EVALUATION_QUARTER is a `segmented-by` edge on the Sales Forecasting concept selected in Step 2 — confusing it with CLOSE_DATE is the most common source of incorrect quarter-end pipeline-to-forecast variance.

selected.label: A deal is 'stalled' or 'ageing' when its DAYS_IN_CURRENT_STAGE exceeds the WON_P90_DAYS benchmark for that stage from PIPELINE_QUALITY_BENCHMARK
selected.description: The PIPELINE_QUALITY_BENCHMARK dataset provides WON_P90_DAYS (90th-percentile days-in-stage for historically won deals) as the health threshold per stage. Opportunities breaching this threshold are surfaced in the Stalled & Ageing Pipe — Cohort 2 dataset.
selected.ai_reasoning: WON_P90_DAYS is a `measured-by` edge on Pipeline Quality & Deal Velocity and DAYS_IN_CURRENT_STAGE is a `derives-from` edge on the core Sales Pipeline concept — this rule links the two and defines when the AI should flag a deal as at-risk.

selected.label: Always apply IS_CURRENT_QTD = TRUE when answering 'how healthy is the pipeline right now?' questions against PIPELINE_QUALITY_AGE_TREND or PIPELINE_QUALITY_END_OF_QUARTER_SNAPSHOT
selected.description: Both pipeline quality datasets contain multi-quarter historical snapshots. Without IS_CURRENT_QTD = TRUE, queries return a mix of current and prior-quarter data, producing misleading deal-age figures.
selected.ai_reasoning: IS_CURRENT_QTD is an explicit `filtered-by` edge on the Pipeline Quality & Deal Velocity concept — it is the primary time-scoping filter the AI must apply for current-state pipeline health questions.

selected.label: Win Rate (RSAC Converted) is revenue-weighted — a single large won deal has more impact than on the deal-count win rate. Do not use the two win rate metrics interchangeably.
selected.description: RSAC (Revenue-Scaled Addressable Conversion) weights each won deal by its value relative to total addressable pipeline. Use Win Rate (Deal Count) for volume/velocity analysis; use RSAC for revenue-quality and territory-level comparisons where deal size varies significantly.
selected.ai_reasoning: Both win rate metrics were selected in Step 4 as `measured-by` edges on the Sales Rep Performance concept — without this distinction the AI will give ambiguous answers when a user simply asks 'what is our win rate?'.

selected.label: Addressable ASP and addressable win rates exclude non-addressable opportunities (renewals, partner-only deals, internal transactions) — they measure new-logo and expansion sales effectiveness only
selected.description: The 'Addressable' qualifier removes opportunities that AEs did not actively compete for, giving a cleaner signal of sales motion effectiveness. Always clarify whether the user wants total or addressable figures before returning ASP or win rate numbers.
selected.ai_reasoning: Addressable ASP is a `measured-by` edge on Sales Rep Performance selected in Step 4 — the AI must understand the addressable filter to avoid inflating or deflating deal-size and conversion benchmarks.

7.question: Several terms in your Sales Pipeline topic could be interpreted in more than one way depending on who is asking. Each pair below identifies a potential confusion point and proposes a default resolution — confirm the ones that apply so the AI disambiguates automatically rather than guessing.

selected.label: "Pipeline" alone → all open (non-closed) opportunities; NOT the Pipe Gen metric and NOT the 'Pipeline' forecast category in SALES_DEFINED_FORECAST
selected.description: The word 'pipeline' carries three distinct meanings in this topic: (1) the full body of open opportunities (Sales Pipeline concept), (2) the Pipe Gen metric measuring new pipeline created in a period, and (3) the SALES_DEFINED_FORECAST value 'Pipeline' denoting early-stage deals in the forecasting model. Default to meaning (1). When context suggests meaning (2) — e.g. 'pipeline generated this quarter' — use CREATED_DATE on the opportunity datasets. When context suggests meaning (3), route to DWH_GTM_OPS_FORECASTING_MODEL filtered on SALES_DEFINED_FORECAST = 'Pipeline'.
selected.ai_reasoning: The Pipe Gen metric, the Sales Pipeline concept, and the SALES_DEFINED_FORECAST 'Pipeline' category all share the same word but produce materially different numbers — this is the single highest-risk lexical collision in the topic.

selected.label: "Win Rate" unqualified → Win Rate (Deal Count), not Win Rate (RSAC Converted)
selected.description: Both win rate metrics are in scope for this topic. When a user asks 'what is our win rate?' without further qualification, the AI should return the deal-count version and surface the RSAC alternative as a note. Use Win Rate (RSAC Converted) only when the user explicitly requests a revenue-weighted, value-adjusted, or RSAC rate.
selected.ai_reasoning: Two win rate metrics were selected in Step 4 with near-identical names — silently defaulting to the revenue-weighted version would surprise most users who expect a simple deal-count ratio and produces a different number.

selected.label: "The forecast" (a number) → Commit + Best Case sum from DWH_GTM_OPS_FORECASTING_MODEL; NOT the SALES_DEFINED_FORECAST column value on individual deal records
selected.description: A user asking 'what is the forecast?' wants an aggregated ARR figure: the sum of opportunities classified as Commit or Best Case for the current EVALUATION_QUARTER. They are not asking for a list of SALES_DEFINED_FORECAST field values per deal. Route aggregate forecast questions to DWH_GTM_OPS_FORECASTING_MODEL grouped by Commit + Best Case; route deal-level category questions to the SALES_DEFINED_FORECAST column itself.
selected.ai_reasoning: SALES_DEFINED_FORECAST is a deal-level classification field, but 'the forecast' is a rolled-up business number — conflating them is the most common cause of incorrect forecast answers and is a gap distinct from the Step 6 Pipeline ≠ Forecast rule.

selected.label: Quarter intent: 'pipeline in Q3' → EVALUATION_QUARTER; 'pipeline created in Q3' → CREATED_DATE; 'pipeline closing in Q3' → CLOSE_DATE
selected.description: Three date fields assign deals to a quarter and each produces a different row count. EVALUATION_QUARTER (in DWH_GTM_OPS_FORECASTING_MODEL) is authoritative for in-quarter forecasting and automatically updates when deals slip. CREATED_DATE is the correct field for Pipe Gen volume. CLOSE_DATE reflects rep-entered expectation but may lag behind for slipped deals. The AI must infer the user's intent from their phrasing before applying any quarter filter.
selected.ai_reasoning: All three date fields appear across the selected datasets and each produces a materially different pipeline number — this rule extends the Step 6 EVALUATION_QUARTER guidance to cover all three date dimensions in one place.

selected.label: "Stalled" deal → DAYS_IN_CURRENT_STAGE > WON_P90_DAYS (quantitative benchmark); NOT informally 'no activity logged in the last N days'
selected.description: The Stalled & Ageing Pipe - Cohort 2 dataset and the PIPELINE_QUALITY_BENCHMARK define stalled using the stage-specific WON_P90_DAYS threshold. Many reps use 'stalled' informally to mean no email, call, or task in the last two weeks. The AI must apply the benchmark-based definition and prompt clarification if the user appears to be asking about activity recency rather than stage age.
selected.ai_reasoning: The WON_P90_DAYS rule was established in Step 6, and both the Stalled & Ageing Pipe and PIPELINE_QUALITY_BENCHMARK datasets were selected in Step 3 — locking in the quantitative definition here prevents the informal interpretation from leaking in.

selected.label: "Conversion rate" in this topic → Pipeline-to-Closed-Won (Win Rate); NOT MQL-to-Pipeline (marketing/SDR funnel conversion)
selected.description: The Marketing Demand Generation & SDR Funnel concept (selected in Step 2) also uses 'conversion' to mean MQL → Pipeline transitions. Within the Sales Pipeline topic, 'conversion rate' should default to deal-level win rate (Pipeline → Closed-Won). Redirect to SDR funnel datasets (GS_MARKETING_FULL_FUNNEL_SDR_* and GS_MARKETING_ANALYSIS_FULL_FUNNEL_SDR_MQL_HISTORY) only when the user explicitly asks about 'MQL conversion', 'SDR conversion', or 'top-of-funnel conversion'.
selected.ai_reasoning: Both Sales Pipeline and Marketing Demand Generation & SDR Funnel concepts are in scope and both legitimately use 'conversion' — without this rule the AI may answer an AE win-rate question using marketing funnel data.

selected.label: "ASP" or "average deal size" → Addressable ASP (excludes non-addressable deals); NOT Bookings ASP (all closed-won deals)
selected.description: Addressable ASP (selected in Step 4) removes renewals, partner-only deals, and internal transactions to measure new-logo and expansion sales effectiveness. Bookings ASP (on the Sales Bookings concept, which is out of scope here) includes all closed-won deals. In this topic, 'ASP' defaults to Addressable ASP for rep-performance and pipeline questions, consistent with the Step 6 addressable definition rule.
selected.ai_reasoning: Both ASP variants exist in the app — Addressable ASP on Sales Rep Performance and Bookings ASP on Sales Bookings — and a plain 'average selling price' question maps to both; this topic's focus on active pipeline warrants the addressable version as the correct default.

selected.label: "Target" / "quota" → PIPE_GEN_GOAL for pipeline questions; BOOKINGS_GOAL for revenue/bookings questions; never a headcount or product-usage quota
selected.description: SFDC_PIPE_GENERATION_BOOKINGS_TARGETS contains both PIPE_GEN_GOAL and BOOKINGS_GOAL. When a user asks 'are we on track to hit target?', the AI must determine whether the question is about pipeline generation or bookings before selecting the correct column. Unqualified 'target' in a pipeline-volume question maps to PIPE_GEN_GOAL; in a closed-revenue question it maps to BOOKINGS_GOAL. The word 'quota' in this topic never refers to headcount hiring or product usage quotas.
selected.ai_reasoning: Both goal columns are in scope via SFDC_PIPE_GENERATION_BOOKINGS_TARGETS (Step 3) and the Target Achieved — Pipe Gen metric (Step 4) — mixing pipeline attainment with bookings attainment in the same answer is a common analytical error.

8.question: How should your Sales Pipeline topic grow over time? Choose an expansion policy that controls how deeply the AI can draw in connected entities — datasets, concepts, and metrics — that aren't explicitly confirmed today but are reachable via graph relationships.

selected.label: Moderate — depth 2, human-confirmed or above  ✦  Recommended
selected.description: Allows the AI to draw in entities up to 2 hops from your confirmed roots, provided they carry at least a human-confirmed trust level. In practice this adds directly adjacent concepts such as Conversation Intelligence (which informs both Sales Pipeline and Sales Rep Performance via the ZRA dataset), GTM Account Coverage & Team Assignment (which informs Sales Rep Performance for territory context), and ICP Account Targeting (which Marketing Demand Generation & SDR Funnel informs for deal-qualification context) — while stopping well short of distant domains like Customer Churn, ARR, or Product Engagement.
selected.ai_reasoning: Moderate expansion is the right balance for a topic this size: the 5 confirmed concepts already have rich, direct graph edges to immediately useful neighbours (Conversation Intelligence for rep coaching, GTM coverage for territory segmentation, ICP targeting for demand-gen qualification) while the 10 step-6 rules and 8 step-7 disambiguation rules provide a strong safety net that prevents conflation with bookings, forecast, or renewal data at depth 2.
